detail: Newell will miss a third consecutive contest due to a left great toe hyperextension. The second-year forward's absence will leave additional playing time for Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

Nelson appeared in four regular-season games for the Nets during the 2025-26 campaign and will link up with the franchise again. He's expected to spend the bulk of his time with their G League affiliate to open the season.

The Hornets initially appeared optimistic about the big man's status for Monday, as he was added to the injury report as questionable Sunday. However, he was downgraded to doubtful earlier in the day Monday and has since been ruled out. The Michigan product will miss his second straight matchup due to right quadriceps tendinopathy.
Williams has yet to appear in a game this season due to a right hamstring strain. His next opportunity to suit up comes Thursday against the Suns.
Awaka's status is uncertain due to a nagging back issue. His availability should be decided at some point closer to tipoff Wednesday.
Collins is in danger of missing his second straight game due to an illness. If he's out again, Jalen Smith and Leonard Miller would likely split Collins' minutes.

Merrill has battled a lingering elbow issue since the preseason. He will now miss a third consecutive contest, with his next opportunity to suit up coming Friday in Miami. While Merrill is sidelined, Craig Porter, Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor should see more minutes.

Johnson will miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign after tallying four points, nine rebounds and one assist in 19 minutes in the first half of a back-to-back set Sunday against Brooklyn. His absence could open up more minutes for Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse behind starting center Daniel Gafford.

Richard has a chance to keep his absence to a one-game minimum with a left thumb UCL tear. It sounds like the guard is opting against surgery and will play with a splint once healthy enough to suit up.

Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

The Pacers continue to monitor the veteran floor general's status after he missed the onset of the campaign. More playing time at point guard would be available for Quenton Jackson if McConnell winds up sitting out Wednesday.

Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Christie will miss his fifth game of the 2026-27 campaign. The 21-year-old rookie has averaged only 6.0 minutes per contest in his five regular-season appearances, so his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation.

Grimes injured his finger in Sunday's game against Detroit and didn't suit up for the 124-114 win over Atlanta on Monday. With Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves (illness) both available, Grimes is expected to head back to the bench. However, another absence could mean more minutes for Sandro Mamukelashvili, Ziaire Williams and Collin Sexton.

Post suffered a concussion during Monday's 118-102 win over the Raptors, and now he will have to clear a series of steps before he's allowed to return to the court. Taylor Hendricks will help pick up the slack while Post is sidelined.
Watford continues to nurse a right ankle sprain. The forward lacks a concrete timetable for a return to the floor.

Hart is sick in addition to dealing with a sore right ankle, so he'll skip Tuesday's game, which will be the first of a back-to-back set. Landry Shamet should continue to start in Hart's absence, and Jordan Clarkson will have the chance for some extra minutes.
Sorber remains in recovery mode due to knee surgery. Until the Thunder update his timetable for a return, Sorber can be deemed week-to-week.

This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

The 25-year-old floor general hasn't played since Oct. 25 due to a right knee bone bruise, though he's "progressing positively" and has returned to on-court activity, according to Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel. The Magic said that Suggs' return will depend on how his knee responds to increased on-court activities, so he can be considered week-to-week until the Magic provide another update on his progress.
Nori did not provide a timetable for Krejci, but it's safe to say that he won't be back soon. His minutes figure to be divvied up amongst Chris Youngblood and Sidy Cissoko.

Vassell missed his first game of the season in Monday's 122-96 victory over the Suns. As a result, Julian Champagnie entered the starting lineup. If Vassell remains sidelined against the Bulls, Champagnie is expected to stay with the first five.

Toronto is likely to re-evaluate Jackson-Davis at some point closer to tipoff Wednesday. Jakob Poeltl would likely handle a larger share of the center minutes if Jackson-Davis isn't feeling well enough to play.
The Raptors are likely to check back in with Murray-Boyles closer to Wednesday's tipoff. Jamison Battle would handle an expanded role in the frontcourt if Murray-Boyles ends up sitting out.
Quickley has a chance Wednesday to end a two-game absence with a hamstring injury. Jamal Shead would have the most to lose from a fantasy perspective if Quickley is able to return.

Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.
